scenes.title: Alerting & Incident Response for Data
scenes.subtitle: From detection to resolution
scenes.narration: Effective alerting and incident response turn a detected data problem into a fast, coordinated fix with minimal downstream impact.

scenes.heading: Traits of good alerts
bullets: Actionable: clearly states what to do
Contextual: includes the failing check and data
scenes.narration: A good alert is actionable, telling the responder exactly what broke and where to look. It is routed to the owner responsible for that dataset rather than a shared void. It carries context like the failing check and sample records, and its severity reflects the real business impact so teams triage correctly.

scenes.heading: The incident response loop
steps: Detect the anomaly and open an incident
Triage severity and assign an owner
Remediate, then write a blameless postmortem
scenes.narration: Response begins when detection opens an incident with a clear record. The team triages severity and assigns a single owner to drive resolution. They diagnose using lineage and logs to trace the root cause, then remediate and close with a blameless postmortem so the same failure does not recur.

scenes.heading: Routing an alert
scenes.narration: This handler assigns severity based on whether the affected dataset is business critical. It builds a payload containing the failing check, the observed value, and the expected threshold so responders start with full context. Critical failures page on-call immediately, while lower-severity ones post to a channel for routine follow-up.

scenes.text: Route the right alert to the right owner with enough context, then follow a repeatable loop to resolution.
scenes.narration: Detection only helps if it reaches someone who can act quickly and confidently. Pair actionable alerts with a clear response process and blameless postmortems to steadily reduce incidents.
